title: Advanced Union and Intersection Patterns knowledge check

questions.prompt: How should code safely use a value whose type is a union?
options: Access every possible field without checking.
Assume the first union member is always present.
Narrow the value using a condition or a discriminator before using member-specific fields.
questions.answer_key: Narrow the value using a condition or a discriminator before using member-specific fields.
questions.explanation: Narrowing establishes which union member applies along a control-flow path.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Advanced Union and Intersection Patterns”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with union transformations and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with union transformations and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Union transformations”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Advanced Union and Intersection Patterns”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check intersection composition, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume handling distributive behavior is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check intersection composition, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Intersection composition”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
